description: Linear and nonlinear filters, edge and gradient operators, convolution and correlation, and binary and grayscale morphology including component labelling and watershed segmentation. These functions work on 2D images, 3D voxel images and plain numeric arrays.

tools.name: GaussianFilter
tools.description: Convolves an image or array with a Gaussian kernel of given radius, producing smooth blurring that suppresses noise. A derivative specification turns it into a smoothed derivative operator. It is the workhorse low-pass filter of image processing.
tools.usage:
GaussianFilter[image, r]
GaussianFilter[image, {r, sigma}]
GaussianFilter[image, r, {dx, dy}]
tools.notes: Gaussian smoothing before differentiation is the standard way to make gradients noise-robust.

tools.name: MeanFilter
tools.description: Replaces each pixel with the mean of its neighborhood, giving simple box blurring. It is fast but produces more ringing than a Gaussian. Use it when a cheap uniform average is enough.

tools.name: MedianFilter
tools.description: Replaces each pixel with the median of its neighborhood, removing salt-and-pepper noise while keeping edges sharp. Unlike mean filtering it does not smear impulses across the image. Use it as the default denoiser for spiky noise.

tools.name: BilateralFilter
tools.description: Smooths an image while preserving edges by weighting neighbors both by spatial distance and by intensity similarity. The second parameter sets how large an intensity difference is still averaged. Use it for denoising photographs and for cartoon-like smoothing.

tools.name: StandardDeviationFilter
tools.description: Computes the local standard deviation in a neighborhood of each pixel, highlighting textured or noisy regions. It is a simple texture and edge-energy detector. Use it for segmentation of smooth versus rough areas.
tools.notes: RangeFilter and GeometricMeanFilter provide related local statistics.

tools.name: RangeFilter
tools.description: Replaces each pixel with the difference between the maximum and minimum values in its neighborhood, the morphological gradient. It gives thick, contrast-driven edge maps. Use it as a fast alternative to gradient filters on binary or high-contrast images.

tools.name: Sharpen
tools.description: Enhances local contrast by adding a scaled high-pass component back to the image, the classic unsharp mask. The radius controls the scale of detail enhanced and the amount controls strength. Over-sharpening produces halos around edges.
tools.usage:
Sharpen[image]
Sharpen[image, r]
Sharpen[image, r, amount]

tools.name: Blur
tools.description: Applies a simple blur of given radius, a convenience wrapper over Gaussian smoothing. Use it when you just want visual softening without tuning kernel parameters. For controlled denoising prefer GaussianFilter or BilateralFilter.

tools.name: EdgeDetect
tools.description: Finds edges in an image and returns a binary edge map, using a Canny-style algorithm by default. The radius sets the smoothing scale and optional thresholds control sensitivity. It is the quickest route from a photo to an outline.
tools.usage:
EdgeDetect[image]
EdgeDetect[image, r]
EdgeDetect[image, r, t]
tools.notes: For a continuous-valued edge strength map use GradientFilter instead of a binarized result.

tools.name: GradientFilter
tools.description: Computes the magnitude of the smoothed image gradient at each pixel, giving a continuous edge-strength map. The radius sets the Gaussian smoothing scale used before differentiation. Use it when you need gradient magnitudes rather than a binary edge decision.
tools.notes: GradientOrientationFilter gives the direction of the gradient, useful for structure tensors and HOG-like features.

tools.name: GradientOrientationFilter
tools.description: Returns the local gradient direction at each pixel, in radians, after Gaussian smoothing. It complements GradientFilter, which gives magnitude only. Use it for orientation histograms, texture analysis and edge linking.

tools.name: LaplacianFilter
tools.description: Applies a discrete Laplacian, a second-derivative operator that responds to intensity curvature. Zero crossings of the result mark edges. It is more noise-sensitive than gradient methods, so it is often combined with smoothing.
tools.notes: LaplacianGaussianFilter combines smoothing and the Laplacian in one pass and is usually the better choice.

tools.name: LaplacianGaussianFilter
tools.description: Convolves an image with a Laplacian-of-Gaussian kernel, giving a scale-selective blob and edge detector. The radius selects the feature size that responds most strongly. It is the basis of classic blob detection.

tools.name: DerivativeFilter
tools.description: Computes arbitrary-order partial derivatives of an image using smoothed difference kernels. Derivative orders are given per dimension, so {1, 0} is the x derivative and {1, 1} a mixed second derivative. Use it to build custom differential operators such as structure tensors.

tools.name: ImageConvolve
tools.description: Convolves an image with an arbitrary kernel matrix, which lets you apply any custom linear filter. Padding controls edge behaviour. Use it to implement textbook kernels such as Sobel, Prewitt or emboss.
tools.usage:
ImageConvolve[image, kernel]
ImageConvolve[image, kernel, Padding -> p]
tools.notes: ImageCorrelate does the same without flipping the kernel, which matters for asymmetric kernels and template matching.

tools.name: ImageCorrelate
tools.description: Correlates an image with a kernel or a template image, optionally with a named distance function such as "NormalizedSquaredEuclideanDistance". This is the basic operation behind template matching. Peaks in the output indicate likely matches.

tools.name: ImageFilter
tools.description: Applies an arbitrary user function to the pixel values in a square neighborhood of every pixel. It generalizes the built-in filters to any local computation. It is flexible but much slower than compiled built-ins, so use those when available.

tools.name: Erosion
tools.description: Performs morphological erosion, shrinking bright regions by the shape of a structuring element. On binary masks it removes small specks and thins objects. The radius or an explicit kernel matrix defines the structuring element.

tools.name: Dilation
tools.description: Performs morphological dilation, growing bright regions by the structuring element. It fills small holes and connects nearby objects. It is the dual of Erosion and the two are usually used together.

tools.name: Opening
tools.description: Applies erosion followed by dilation, removing small bright features while preserving the size of larger ones. It is the standard way to clean speckle noise from a binary mask. The structuring element determines which features survive.

tools.name: Closing
tools.description: Applies dilation followed by erosion, filling small dark gaps and holes without growing objects overall. It is the complement of Opening. Use it to close broken outlines before component analysis.

tools.name: TopHatTransform
tools.description: Subtracts the morphological opening from the image, isolating bright features smaller than the structuring element. It is the standard technique for correcting uneven illumination before thresholding. BottomHatTransform does the same for dark features.

tools.name: BottomHatTransform
tools.description: Subtracts the image from its morphological closing, highlighting dark features smaller than the structuring element. Use it to find dark spots, cracks or text on a bright background. It pairs with TopHatTransform for background correction.

tools.name: MorphologicalComponents
tools.description: Labels each connected component of a binary image with a distinct integer, returning an integer array. Connectivity and a minimum component size can be specified. It is the entry point for counting and measuring objects.
tools.notes: Feed the result to ComponentMeasurements to get areas, centroids and shape descriptors.

tools.name: ComponentMeasurements
tools.description: Computes geometric and intensity properties of labelled image components, such as area, centroid, bounding box, eccentricity and mean intensity. Results come back as rules from component label to value, and criteria can filter components. It is the core measurement tool for quantitative image analysis.

parameters.name: crit
parameters.description: Criterion selecting which components to keep, e.g. #Area > 50 &.

tools.name: WatershedComponents
tools.description: Segments an image with the watershed transform, treating intensity as elevation and flooding from markers. Supplying markers avoids the over-segmentation that the unseeded version produces. It is the classic method for separating touching objects such as cells or coins.
tools.usage:
WatershedComponents[image]
WatershedComponents[image, marker]
WatershedComponents[image, marker, Method -> "Immersion"]

tools.name: ImageForestingComponents
tools.description: Segments an image using the image foresting transform, growing regions from seed markers along minimum-cost paths. It is well suited to interactive segmentation where the user clicks foreground and background points. Distance functions and connectivity are configurable.

tools.name: ClusteringComponents
tools.description: Segments an image or array into a given number of clusters by grouping pixel values, effectively a color or intensity quantization segmentation. It returns an integer label array. Use it for unsupervised region segmentation when spatial connectivity is not required.
tools.usage:
ClusteringComponents[image]
ClusteringComponents[image, n]
ClusteringComponents[image, n, level]
tools.notes: Method -> "KMeans" or "MeanShift" can be given; FindClusters offers the same algorithms on generic data.

tools.name: DistanceTransform
tools.description: Computes, for each foreground pixel, the distance to the nearest background pixel. Peaks of the transform mark object centers, which makes it the usual marker generator for watershed segmentation. Several distance metrics are supported.

tools.name: MorphologicalBinarize
tools.description: Binarizes an image using two thresholds with hysteresis, so that weak pixels are kept only when connected to strong ones. This produces cleaner masks than a single global threshold on noisy images. Thresholds can be chosen automatically.
tools.notes: LocalAdaptiveBinarize is preferable when illumination varies smoothly across the frame.

tools.name: Thinning
tools.description: Iteratively thins a binary image until objects become one-pixel-wide skeletons, preserving connectivity. Use it to reduce strokes, traces or vessels to centerlines. The number of iterations can be limited.
tools.notes: SkeletonTransform gives a distance-weighted skeleton; Pruning removes short spurs from either result.

tools.name: SkeletonTransform
tools.description: Computes the morphological skeleton of a binary image, the set of centers of maximal inscribed disks. It preserves topology and can be used to reconstruct the original shape. Use it for shape analysis and medial-axis extraction.

tools.name: Pruning
tools.description: Removes short branches (spurs) from a skeletonized binary image, leaving only the main structure. The number of pruning iterations controls how long a branch must be to survive. Use it to clean noisy skeletons before graph extraction.

tools.name: FillingTransform
tools.description: Fills holes in an image, meaning connected dark regions that are completely surrounded by brighter pixels. On binary masks it closes interior voids left by thresholding. A depth argument controls which holes are filled.

tools.name: Inpaint
tools.description: Reconstructs image content in regions marked by a mask, using information from the surrounding pixels. Several methods are available, from fast marching to texture synthesis. Use it to remove scratches, text overlays or unwanted objects.

tools.name: ImageDeconvolve
tools.description: Recovers a sharper image by deconvolving a known or estimated point spread function, undoing blur. Regularized methods such as Richardson-Lucy and Tikhonov control noise amplification. Use it for motion or defocus blur where the PSF can be modelled.

tools.name: ImageEffect
tools.description: Applies a named artistic or simulation effect to an image, such as noise, embossing, oil painting, solarization or vignetting. Effects take parameters as a list with the name first. It is also a convenient way to synthesize noisy test images.

tools.name: Colorize
tools.description: Maps the integer labels or scalar values of an array or image to distinct colors, making segmentation results readable. A color scheme or explicit color rules can be given. Use it immediately after any component-labelling function.

tools.name: MaxDetect
tools.description: Finds regional maxima of an image, returning a binary image of the peak regions. An h-value suppresses maxima that are not prominent enough, which controls over-detection. It is commonly used to generate watershed markers.
tools.notes: MinDetect is the corresponding operation for regional minima.
